# Kingdom login and session: is this moment mine?

## What this region is

How KCP signs a machine in to one Kingdom and keeps that session: which Kingdom and which local directory, the three logins plus logout and status, the rules for Kingdom API tokens and printed secrets, and the /api/v1/me/overview read behind kcp map.

## What it exists for

- Work out which Kingdom to call and where KCP keeps its files
- Get Signets onto this machine's key
- See or clear what this machine holds
- Choose the login command a person runs
- Turn Kingdom's /me/overview into the owner->integration map
- Pick out Signets, integrations and families from the overview

## When this is not your domain

These mention this region's words but belong elsewhere; the answer is no, and the region named answers instead.

- the user passes an integration id with -i and it isn't a UUID → command-proxy
- map the gh binary to the github provider → command-proxy
- pick which held Signet runs this railway command → command-proxy
- add a new kcp subcommand to the help text → kcp-scope-and-cli
- is the git credential helper built yet → kcp-scope-and-cli
